transcription.text: Hi, welcome to the EEVblog, an electronics engineering video blog of interest to anyone
involved in electronics design. I'm your host, Dave Jones. Hi, it's product review time again.
I thought I'd do a quick review on these funky Samson 4i USB studio monitor speakers. Now,
normally I wouldn't review a set of speakers because this is an electronics show,
not an audiophile show, but these are the USB Connect ones, so they've got to have some
electronics in them. So I thought I'd crack them open, see what's in there. So it's more of a
teardown than a review, really. You won't get any audiophile wank words out of me. Maybe.
The reason I went looking for a pair of USB studio monitor speakers is because, as you know,
I do a lot of video editing. Sometimes some of my videos can have hundreds of clips in them,
and that takes many, many hours to edit. And normally I do it with the headphones. Coincidentally,
these are Samson as well. SR850, if you're after a decent, good quality pair of studio monitor

speakers as well. But yeah, the dynamic range of speakers is much better. You stick them on,
and they help seal out external noises, and then you can hear during video editing all the little

the screws out, maybe. No, I reckon. Oh yeah, here it comes.
Yep. Whee! Yes! Exactly what I thought.
Yep. Ta-da!
There you go. There's the wiring and the electronics. And at first glance, I'm quite
